title: Lockdown Scrim — SOC2 field notes (Ashira)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, messy running notes from a simulated "scrim" I ran w/ Noah + Maya to exercise SOC2 evidence paths for Private/VPC + Dedicated capacity. Not polished — intentionally raw so we can capture gaps.

Context:
- Running a short tabletop -> then an evidence-collection run across infra (GCP) + control plane logs (Redwood CP).
- Focus areas: key management & rotation, admin access reviews, deployment approvals, incident logging/retention, separation of duties for deploys to Private.

What we exercised (scenario):
- Scenario: customer requests emergency rollback for a private deployment (on-prem) after noisy inference leading to PII exposure suspicion. Ops must: 1) revoke any exposed keys, 2) snapshot evidence from audit logs, 3) ensure rollback approved by product security + legal, 4) communicate to customer and trigger postmortem.

Quick wins observed:
- Audit logs for control plane (redwood-cp-audit) contain fine-grained entries with user_id and request_id -> good for traceability. Example entry pattern: "ts user action resource request_id".
- GCP IAM activity shows resource changes (instance templates, firewall rules) but we need clearer linking from CP request_id -> cloud operation id.
- KMS usage audit exists but rotation records are in a different project (kms-ops) and not cross-linked. Need a view that correlates key_id -> service account usage.

Control mapping notes (draft):
- CC: Access reviews (periodic) -> source: admin console monthly export (admin/audit-export). Action: schedule a quarterly drift check for Service Accounts with Owner role.
- CC: Change approvals for infra (PR + JIRA approval) -> source: GH PR + JIRA ticket. Gap: emergency rollbacks sometimes bypass PR approvals (Slack approvals). Need documented exception workflow + ticketing requirement.
- CC: Key custody -> KMS keys are in project ops-kms; Private deployments also use customer-managed keys via HSM in a partner data center. Map: control -> evidence: KMS rotation logs + HSM attestation report.

Evidence hunting checklist (what I pulled during scrim):
- Redwood CP audit trace for the rollback request: request_id=rb-20260211-58f2 -> pulled JSON export to /tmp/evidence-rb-58f2.json (store in secure bucket).
- GCP operation id for instance deletion: op-0a3b -> cloudaudit.googleapis.com entries (pulled).
- KMS key use around that TTL window: key-9x rotation events at 2026-02-10T23:49Z (rotation policy attached).
- Vault (secrets) access logs: svc-deploy consumed secret secret/model-credentials 2026-02-11T00:02Z.
- Slack thread link where emergency approval occurred (private channel): https://redwood.slack.com/archives/CP93XXXXX/p1676100000000 -> need to screenshot and ingest into evidence store.

Open questions / unresolved risks:
- How do we prove separation of duties for emergency workflows that are approved in Slack? We need a documented exception flow that creates a JIRA ticket automatically and forces a post-facto audit event.
- Are HSM attestation reports retained for the required SOC2 window? Where is retention policy defined?
- For Private deployments using customer-managed keys, do we have a reproducible chain showing we cannot access plaintext keys? Need statement + procedure for evidence.
- Is the backup retention policy for CP logs long enough? We saw CP logs older than 90 days archived to long-term storage; confirm indexing/searchability for >90 days.

Draft control language snippets (for mapping doc):
- "All emergency deployment rollbacks must be accompanied by a recorded approval that is linked to a ticket and captured in the audit trail within 24 hours."
- "Service accounts with elevated roles must be reviewed quarterly; any owner-level access for non-human principals must have a compensating control and a rotation schedule."

Small tactical fixes to implement quickly (owner -> due):
- auto-create JIRA when someone posts "/emergency-rollback" in #ops-urgent (Noah) -> due 2026-02-26
- add request_id -> GCP operation id crosswalk to the CP logger (Maya) -> due 2026-03-05
- centralize KMS rotation events into a single ops-runbook view + add retention metadata (me) -> due 2026-03-01

Evidence retention & classifiers (notes):
- CP audit exports -> archived to gs://redwood-evidence/cp-audit/YYYY-MM (retention policy 3 years) but index snapshot only kept for 180 days. Need to push index snapshots to long-term search.
- Slack screenshots -> currently manual; propose ingestion pipeline that attaches Slack message + permalink + screenshot to a secured evidence artifact with metadata (ticket id, request_id).

Snippets / CLI cheats (for next run):
- gcloud logging read "resource.type=project AND protoPayload.requestId=\"rb-20260211-58f2\"" --project=redwood-cp --limit=100 --format=json > evidence/rb-58f2-ops.json
- jq '.[] | {ts:.timestamp, user:.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, action:.protoPayload.methodName}' evidence/rb-58f2-ops.json > evidence/rb-58f2-summary.json

Postmortem template notes (quick):
- tl;dr (one line)
- timeline with request_ids and cloud op ids
- what evidence artifacts were collected (list + location)
- root cause hypothesis + controls that failed
- action items w/ owners + due dates

Possible follow-ups for compliance thread:
- Run a focused exercise just for KMS/HSM attestation: invite infra, security, and legal; get an HSM vendor rep to explain retention.
- Build a demo of the auto-ticketing slash command and test it during next oncall shift.

Notes-to-self (rambling):
- Keep the scrim cadence regular (every 6 weeks) and vary the scenario (data exfiltration, misconfigured firewall, accidental wide-access model deploy).
- Need a short checklist for customer communication templates (legal + CS quick text) so oncall doesn't improvise.

Attachments / where I dropped artifacts during run:
- /tmp/evidence-rb-58f2.json (moved to gs://redwood-evidence/temp/rb-58f2.json)
- screenshots saved to drive -> TODO: move to evidence bucket and redact PII

Next meeting: 2026-02-25 10:00 PT (scrim retro)
Action owners: assign in JIRA then link here.

End of scratch notes. Intend to fold the above into a tidy "control-mapping-for-emergency-rollbacks" doc once we confirm HSM retention and auto-ticketing feasibility.
